=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics, AUD 24,000,000, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law

## Preliminary point: the Seller's labels and "FINAL" framing

The Seller's covering note marks most clauses [STANDARD], says they were "cleared by both sides," and asks the reviewer to look only at [OPEN] items. There are no [OPEN] items, so following the note would mean reviewing nothing. **I have not relied on these labels.** Unless the deal team confirms that particular points were in fact agreed at principal level, every position below should be treated as open.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (paragraphs 2–6, 8 and 10) also confirms that several "addressed" items are unresolved. That contradicts the covering note.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) on general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1). Under cl 12.3/9.3 the cap applies to *all* Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general cap, such as 30–50% (AUD 7.2m–12m), or 20% only if backed by W&I cover. Fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and fraud should sit outside the general cap, capped at 100% of price (or uncapped for fraud).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted. Counter at 40% for general warranties, with carve-outs.** Reason: about 30% of revenue (Bluefen), AUD 3.2m of debt, an unresolved privacy incident and an IP chain gap make the risk concentration too high for a 20% cap applying to everything.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000 (about 0.1%). Basket AUD 250,000 (about 1.04%), and only the excess is recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis around AUD 10,000. A **tipping** basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120,000) so the first dollar is recoverable once the threshold is hit. Related claims aggregate for de minimis. Neither threshold applies to fundamental, tax, specific indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** Reason: a deductible basket combined with a de minimis that excludes small claims lets the Seller keep a meaningful slice of genuine loss. Several low-value privacy or supplier claims could fall entirely below the de minimis.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default extends this to tax, title and indemnities.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties (at least two full audit cycles post-Completion). Tax: the statutory amendment period plus 6 months, or 5–7 years. Fundamental/title: 6–7 years, matching the NSW Limitation Act 1969 contract period. Specific indemnities should run for their own tailored periods, for example privacy at a minimum of 3 years. The default should be reversed so limits apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the default rule. Counter at 24 months for general warranties.** Reason: 18 months for everything would cut off the tax and title claims that typically emerge last.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties take the same cap and time limit as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share capital, no encumbrances, insolvency) capped at 100% of price, outside the de minimis and basket, not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge, with a 6–7 year survival.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Reason: if title fails, the Buyer has lost the whole AUD 24m. A cap of AUD 4.8m on that warranty is not a simplification; it is a reallocation of the core deal risk to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out. The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out disapplying every limitation, the exclusive remedy, non-reliance and Buyer knowledge for fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers or the Company's management. Non-reliance should also expressly preserve the specific warranties and disclosure statements.
- **Recommendation:** **Insist. Treat as non-negotiable.** Reason: NSW courts are unlikely to enforce limitations against a party's own fraud anyway, but the express carve-out removes argument and also captures wilful concealment and management fraud, which may not otherwise be covered.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Warranties qualified only by matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter against specific warranties, with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely financial impact. The data room should not be generally disclosed, or at most disclosed only to the extent fairly disclosed, with a USB copy and index annexed. Disclosure should never qualify fundamental warranties, the tax covenant or specific indemnities. Public records disclosure should be limited to ASIC/PPSR searches conducted by the Buyer on a stated date.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject general disclosure.** Reason: blanket data room disclosure combined with the knowledge qualifier would neutralise most warranties. DL 1.4, which says nothing admits materiality or required action, makes the specific disclosures insufficient for fair disclosure in any event.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3). This is constructive knowledge.
- **Buyer wants:** An express pro-sandbagging clause: Buyer knowledge, investigation or due diligence does not reduce any claim. The fallback is a qualifier limited to the **actual** knowledge of named individuals on the Buyer deal team, excluding advisers, constructive or imputed knowledge, and never applying to fundamental, tax, specific indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter pro-sandbagging, with the named-individual actual-knowledge fallback.** Reason: the Seller's drafting means any issue found in diligence, including every issue in this memo, defeats the claim. That would make the specific indemnities pointless.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent. DL para 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A condition precedent of unconditional written consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - Evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.
  - No adverse amendment to contract terms.
  - The CP waivable only by the Buyer.
  - An "all reasonable endeavours" obligation on the Seller.
  - A Buyer right to terminate if the CP is not satisfied by the sunset date.
  - A fallback price adjustment or specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or reprices within, say, 12 months.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter. Make this a full CP.** Reason: Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. Consent that is still subject to unmet conditions is not consent.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion." DL para 3 says the facility is not repaid, no discharge has been provided, and there is a change-control trigger (cl 8.1).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A payout letter before Completion.
  - The facility (about AUD 3.2m plus interest and break costs) paid directly from the price at Completion as Debt.
  - Executed deeds of release and discharge, plus PPSR financing change statements, delivered **at** Completion.
  - Riverlark's confirmation that the cl 8.1 change-control default will not be called before payout.
  - A specific indemnity for any residual amounts.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-Completion release.** Reason: the deal is debt-free. Paying AUD 24m while security remains over the target, and while a change-control default exists, is unacceptable.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Bonuses of AUD 420,000 (DD-005) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. DL para 5 does not address payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses plus all on-costs treated as Transaction Costs/Debt-like Items and deducted from the price. On-costs include employer superannuation (12% SG), NSW payroll tax, workers' compensation and any PAYG withholding mechanics. Payment should go through Company payroll at Completion, funded by the Seller, with a specific indemnity outside the cap and basket.
- **Recommendation:** **Insist on a price deduction.** Reason: the obligation sits with the Company, which the Buyer will own. Unless the amount is itemised in the funds flow, the Buyer pays about AUD 420,000 plus roughly AUD 70,000+ in on-costs twice.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl 11.1). DL para 4 says DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee, AUD 180,000 is shown as open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - As a CP or Completion deliverable, evidence of cleared payment (Seller-funded or deducted) **and** an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, including moral rights consents.
  - Failing that, a specific indemnity covering all loss from the Company not owning the SOW3 materials, including third-party infringement claims, re-development costs and lost revenue.
  - That indemnity uncapped (or at 100%), outside the basket, unaffected by disclosure or knowledge, and supported by a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as inadequate.** Reason: paying AUD 180,000 does not by itself cure title. Until the assignment is executed, the Company may not own core product IP, and the loss from that could be far larger than the fee.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6 / Sch 6). DL para 6 notes about 1,240 records sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability are not established, and no loss amount is given.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A pre-Completion covenant for the Seller to complete a forensic investigation, with the report provided to the Buyer.
  - Written confirmation of the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches assessment and of any OAIC or individual notifications.
  - A specific indemnity for regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, customer claims and contract claims, outside the cap and basket, surviving at least 3 years.
  - A retention.
  - Privacy/data warranties not qualified by DL para 6.
- **Recommendation:** **Insist on a specific indemnity and retention.** Reason: the incident pre-dates 22 September 2026. As of 5 November 2026, the 30-day assessment window under the Privacy Act 1988 (s 26WH) has likely elapsed. That creates possible compliance exposure the Seller has not addressed. **Flag for urgent confirmation.**

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL para 8 says they are "related" and should be "read together," but does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Full copies and an explanation of why one supplier arrangement was split into three.
  - Confirmation of whether this avoided any approval threshold, conduct-of-business restriction or related-party rule.
  - Warranties that the renewals are on arm's-length terms and terminable without penalty.
  - Any prepaid, accrued or unavoidable amounts for post-Completion periods not in the business plan treated as Debt-like Items.
  - Buyer consent required for any further renewals before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the ordinary-course characterisation without diligence.** Reason: three identical related contracts, flagged by the Seller to be read together, look like a threshold-splitting pattern. That needs explaining before the Buyer absorbs AUD 330,000.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13). Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance cover "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Defined, separate claim categories, each with its own regime:
  - General warranties
  - Fundamental warranties
  - Tax covenant/indemnity
  - Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Riverlark, Bluefen)
  - Covenant/undertaking breaches
  - Completion accounts/price adjustment
  - Fraud

  Limitations should apply only to the category expressly stated, with the default reversed.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the catch-all.** Reason: without separation, every protection in items 4–13 collapses into the 20% cap, the AUD 250k deductible and the 18-month limit. This is the structural point that ties the whole package together.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL para 10 expressly notes that the Buyer has not done its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The Buyer's own ASIC company extract and historical searches.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
  - A review of the constitution and any shareholders' agreement for pre-emption or drag rights.
  - Confirmation of no options, convertible notes, SAFEs or ESOP entitlements.
  - Original share certificates, a signed share transfer form, and waivers of pre-emptive rights as Completion deliverables.
  - Full title and capitalisation warranties as fundamental warranties (see item 4).
- **Recommendation:** **Do not rely on the register alone.** Reason: a self-maintained register is the Seller's own record. It does not prove the absence of encumbrances, unissued entitlements or registration errors.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, AUD 250k basket, 18 months, general disclosure, knowledge qualifier).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone tax covenant/indemnity, pound-for-pound, for pre-Completion tax (income tax, payroll tax including on the item 10 bonuses, GST, PAYG, superannuation guarantee charge). Capped at 100% of price, outside the basket, with survival to the statutory amendment period plus 6 months. Not qualified by disclosure. Buyer conduct of claims, subject to reasonable Seller consultation.
  - **IP:** Warranties on ownership of all Company IP (including the Ironquay materials), employee and contractor assignments, open-source compliance and non-infringement. Ownership warranties should carry a higher cap, at or near fundamental status, with a 3–4 year survival.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled." Treat both as open.** Reason: for a SaaS target, IP ownership and tax/super compliance carry the most value, and an 18-month window will close before most ATO reviews begin.

---

## Priority order for the mark-up
1. **Category separation (014) and fraud carve-out (005).** These are structural; without them, the other protections fail.
2. **Riverlark (009), bonuses (010), Bluefen (008).** These are funds-flow and CP items that must be fixed before signing.
3. **Privacy incident (012) and Ironquay IP (011).** These need specific indemnities and a retention. Confirm the NDB assessment status urgently.
4. **Disclosure (006) and Buyer knowledge (007).**
5. **Fundamental/title (004, 015) and tax/IP (016).**
6. **Cap, basket and time limit (001–003).** These are commercial levers that can be traded once the structure is secured.
7. **Sandbar (013).** Requires diligence follow-up.

**Not in scope but worth noting:** the office lease (DL para 7, notification only) and Mossvale (DL para 9, assignment restriction). Both seem low risk, but counsel should read the actual clauses to confirm that a share sale does not trigger them, for example through deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording.

**Caveats:** This review is based only on the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA text. Percentages are calculated against AUD 24m. Counter-positions are opening suggestions and should be calibrated to the Buyer's risk appetite and any W&I strategy. Confirm with the deal principals whether any point was genuinely agreed before treating it as reopened.

  - The CP waivable only by the Buyer.
  - An "all reasonable endeavours" obligation on the Seller.
  - A Buyer right to terminate if the CP is not satisfied by the sunset date.
  - A fallback price adjustment or specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or reprices within, say, 12 months.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter. Make this a full CP.** Reason: Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. Consent that is still subject to unmet conditions is not consent.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion." DL para 3 says the facility is not repaid, no discharge has been provided, and there is a change-control trigger (cl 8.1).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A payout letter before Completion.
  - The facility (about AUD 3.2m plus interest and break costs) paid directly from the price at Completion as Debt.
  - Executed deeds of release and discharge, plus PPSR financing change statements, delivered **at** Completion.
  - Riverlark's confirmation that the cl 8.1 change-control default will not be called before payout.
  - A specific indemnity for any residual amounts.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-Completion release.** Reason: the deal is debt-free. Paying AUD 24m while security remains over the target, and while a change-control default exists, is unacceptable.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Bonuses of AUD 420,000 (DD-005) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. DL para 5 does not address payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses plus all on-costs treated as Transaction Costs/Debt-like Items and deducted from the price. On-costs include employer superannuation (12% SG), NSW payroll tax, workers' compensation and any PAYG withholding mechanics. Payment should go through Company payroll at Completion, funded by the Seller, with a specific indemnity outside the cap and basket.
- **Recommendation:** **Insist on a price deduction.** Reason: the obligation sits with the Company, which the Buyer will own. Unless the amount is itemised in the funds flow, the Buyer pays about AUD 420,000 plus roughly AUD 70,000+ in on-costs twice.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl 11.1). DL para 4 says DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee, AUD 180,000 is shown as open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - As a CP or Completion deliverable, evidence of cleared payment (Seller-funded or deducted) **and** an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, including moral rights consents.
  - Failing that, a specific indemnity covering all loss from the Company not owning the SOW3 materials, including third-party infringement claims, re-development costs and lost revenue.
  - That indemnity uncapped (or at 100%), outside the basket, unaffected by disclosure or knowledge, and supported by a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as inadequate.** Reason: paying AUD 180,000 does not by itself cure title. Until the assignment is executed, the Company may not own core product IP, and the loss from that could be far larger than the fee.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6 / Sch 6). DL para 6 notes about 1,240 records sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability are not established, and no loss amount is given.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A pre-Completion covenant for the Seller to complete a forensic investigation, with the report provided to the Buyer.
  - Written confirmation of the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches assessment and of any OAIC or individual notifications.
  - A specific indemnity for regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, customer claims and contract claims, outside the cap and basket, surviving at least 3 years.
  - A retention.
  - Privacy/data warranties not qualified by DL para 6.
- **Recommendation:** **Insist on a specific indemnity and retention.** Reason: the incident pre-dates 22 September 2026. As of 5 November 2026, the 30-day assessment window under the Privacy Act 1988 (s 26WH) has likely elapsed. That creates possible compliance exposure the Seller has not addressed. **Flag for urgent confirmation.**

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL para 8 says they are "related" and should be "read together," but does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Full copies and an explanation of why one supplier arrangement was split into three.
  - Confirmation of whether this avoided any approval threshold, conduct-of-business restriction or related-party rule.
  - Warranties that the renewals are on arm's-length terms and terminable without penalty.
  - Any prepaid, accrued or unavoidable amounts for post-Completion periods not in the business plan treated as Debt-like Items.
  - Buyer consent required for any further renewals before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the ordinary-course characterisation without diligence.** Reason: three identical related contracts, flagged by the Seller to be read together, look like a threshold-splitting pattern. That needs explaining before the Buyer absorbs AUD 330,000.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13). Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance cover "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Defined, separate claim categories, each with its own regime:
  - General warranties
  - Fundamental warranties
  - Tax covenant/indemnity
  - Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Riverlark, Bluefen)
  - Covenant/undertaking breaches
  - Completion accounts/price adjustment
  - Fraud

  Limitations should apply only to the category expressly stated, with the default reversed.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the catch-all.** Reason: without separation, every protection in items 4–13 collapses into the 20% cap, the AUD 250k deductible and the 18-month limit. This is the structural point that ties the whole package together.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL para 10 expressly notes that the Buyer has not done its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The Buyer's own ASIC company extract and historical searches.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
  - A review of the constitution and any shareholders' agreement for pre-emption or drag rights.
  - Confirmation of no options, convertible notes, SAFEs or ESOP entitlements.
  - Original share certificates, a signed share transfer form, and waivers of pre-emptive rights as Completion deliverables.
  - Full title and capitalisation warranties as fundamental warranties (see item 4).
- **Recommendation:** **Do not rely on the register alone.** Reason: a self-maintained register is the Seller's own record. It does not prove the absence of encumbrances, unissued entitlements or registration errors.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, AUD 250k basket, 18 months, general disclosure, knowledge qualifier).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone tax covenant/indemnity, pound-for-pound, for pre-Completion tax (income tax, payroll tax including on the item 10 bonuses, GST, PAYG, superannuation guarantee charge). Capped at 100% of price, outside the basket, with survival to the statutory amendment period plus 6 months. Not qualified by disclosure. Buyer conduct of claims, subject to reasonable Seller consultation.
  - **IP:** Warranties on ownership of all Company IP (including the Ironquay materials), employee and contractor assignments, open-source compliance and non-infringement. Ownership warranties should carry a higher cap, at or near fundamental status, with a 3–4 year survival.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled." Treat both as open.** Reason: for a SaaS target, IP ownership and tax/super compliance carry the most value, and an 18-month window will close before most ATO reviews begin.

## Priority order for the mark-up
1. **Category separation (014) and fraud carve-out (005).** These are structural; without them, the other protections fail.
2. **Riverlark (009), bonuses (010), Bluefen (008).** These are funds-flow and CP items that must be fixed before signing.
3. **Privacy incident (012) and Ironquay IP (011).** These need specific indemnities and a retention. Confirm the NDB assessment status urgently.
4. **Disclosure (006) and Buyer knowledge (007).**
5. **Fundamental/title (004, 015) and tax/IP (016).**
6. **Cap, basket and time limit (001–003).** These are commercial levers that can be traded once the structure is secured.
7. **Sandbar (013).** Requires diligence follow-up.

**Not in scope but worth noting:** the office lease (DL para 7, notification only) and Mossvale (DL para 9, assignment restriction). Both seem low risk, but counsel should read the actual clauses to confirm that a share sale does not trigger them, for example through deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording.

**Caveats:** This review is based only on the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA text. Percentages are calculated against AUD 24m. Counter-positions are opening suggestions and should be calibrated to the Buyer's risk appetite and any W&I strategy. Confirm with the deal principals whether any point was genuinely agreed before treating it as reopened.
